clue.text: Seek a criminal now the railway line has been laid

parts.note: a railway line is the track the trains run on
something laid has been put down flat

explanation.surface: A hunt for a crook begins as soon as the new railway is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a building project; in fact the railway line is TRACK and being laid puts it DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue a wanted person until they are found is the phrasal verb meaning to hunt someone out.

clue.text: What angry men hit if they go through the ceiling?

definitions.text: What angry men hit if they go through the ceiling?

parts.words: What angry men hit if they go through the ceiling?
parts.note: an angry person is said to hit the top of the house, an idiom for losing one's temper, which a literal leap through the ceiling would also do

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for flying into a rage names the top covering of a building, which lies just above a ceiling.

clue.text: Essential in 1500 that nothing left for reformation of the curia

indicators.note: the shuffled letters of the clue's curia sit inside the Roman numerals, so 'in' places one piece within the other

parts.note: 1500 with its nought (nothing) left out is 150, which in Roman numerals is C (100) and L (50)

indicators.note: a reformation reshapes something, so the letters of the clue's curia are rearranged

explanation.surface: A historical note on how the papal court was reformed in the sixteenth century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformation of' turns CURIA into RUCIA, and 'in' puts it between C and L: 1500 without its final 0 (nothing) is 150, CL in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crucial is vital or indispensable, a synonym of essential.

clue.text: Fishing boat that cruises around aimlessly

definitions.meaning: a vessel that fishes with drift nets
a person who wanders from place to place without purpose

explanation.definitionFit: A drift-net vessel and a rootless wanderer share the same name, both moving with the current.

clue.text: Unco-operative habit

definitions.meaning: an unco-operative person says they will not, contracted with an apostrophe
an old word for a custom or usual practice

explanation.definitionFit: The contraction of 'will not' expresses refusal, while the same letters without an apostrophe are an old noun for custom.

clue.text: One well-read and well-acquainted with legal matters

definitions.text: One well-read and well-acquainted with legal matters

parts.words: One well-read and well-acquainted with legal matters
parts.note: the words describe a scholarly companion, but together they point to the courtroom phrase by which barristers refer to one another

explanation.surface: A description of a bookish person who knows the law well.
explanation.walkthrough: In British courts barristers politely call each other by this two-word title; 'well-read' and 'well-acquainted' gloss each word.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtroom form of address used between barristers pairs a word for scholarly with a word for a companion.

clue.text: Ron's trip I can't translate into a written record

indicators.note: to translate is to turn into another form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe gives no letter, leaving the name and its s
the apostrophe gives no letter

explanation.surface: Ron's journey is in a language that cannot be put into writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translate' signals the anagram of RONSTRIPICANT; 'into' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A transcription is a written copy of something spoken or recorded, so it is a written record.

clue.text: Our violent Ray disposed of a violent political character

indicators.note: the letters are disposed, that is set out afresh, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thuggish man called Ray is got rid of by a militant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed of' reads as 'got rid of' but signals the letters of OUR VIOLENT RAY arranged anew.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolutionary is a person who uses force to overthrow a government, a violent political figure.

clue.text: Horrible debts acquired by a worried Croat

indicators.note: the debts are picked up by the jumbled Croat, so they follow it
worried means shaken about, so the letters of the clue's Croat are jumbled

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to repay, so debts

explanation.surface: An anxious Croatian man runs up debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' turns CROAT into ATROC, and 'acquired by' adds the IOUS after it; the 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means appallingly bad or dreadful, so it means horrible.

clue.text: We shall shortly be taking a mixed gin, so here's health!

parts.note: we shall shortened to its contraction gives we'll, written without the apostrophe
taken as written

indicators.note: mixed means stirred up, so the letters of the clue's gin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker proposing a toast over a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' gives ING from GIN; 'taking a' and 'so here's' are link words around the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellbeing is the state of being healthy and comfortable, so it means health.

clue.text: Sweet and sour

definitions.meaning: a pastry dessert with a filling
sharp to the taste, acid

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a fruit pastry pudding, while the adjective describes a sharp, acidic taste.

clue.text: Point two underlined in Mr Fawkes's November diary?

definitions.meaning: 0.2 as a fraction is one part in five

definitions.text: underlined in Mr Fawkes's November diary?
definitions.meaning: Guy Fawkes's Gunpowder Plot was set for the 5th of November, the date he would mark

explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes tried to blow up Parliament on 5 November 1605, still marked in Britain as Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Decimal 0.2 equals one part in five, and the plot date was the day numbered five in November.

clue.text: One time some time ago

definitions.meaning: on a single occasion
formerly, in the past

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means on a single occasion and also formerly, at some point in the past.

clue.text: Father a friend of the pope

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A priest who is close to the pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' and 'friend of the pope' suggest a churchman; the 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Papal is the adjective for anything belonging to the pontiff.

clue.text: Befuddle theologian in the drink

indicators.note: the theologian is placed within the drink, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar gets muddled after too much beer.
explanation.walkthrough: DD (Doctor of Divinity) is the usual crossword theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to confuse or muddle, a synonym of befuddle.

clue.text: Taking everything into account it is the best working habit

definitions.meaning: all things considered, as an adverb
a habit is a garment, and one worn for work is a protective coat or dungarees

explanation.walkthrough: 'It is the best' is a link phrase hinting at the adjective sense (the best over all others); 'habit' means clothing, not a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means in general or all told; as a noun it is a protective garment worn over clothes for work.

clue.text: The root of all reformist policies

definitions.meaning: from Latin radix, a root, as in a mathematical or word root
favouring sweeping political change

explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from the Latin for root and names a root in maths, and also describes a politician seeking thorough change.

clue.text: Blow up the anti-monetarist policy

definitions.meaning: fill with air, swell
monetarists aim to control the money supply; the opposite course lets prices and money swell

explanation.definitionFit: To pump up a tyre or balloon, and the economic course of expanding money and prices that monetarists oppose.

clue.text: No longer sufficient to serve as an illustration

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
ample means enough, sufficient

explanation.surface: Something that used to be adequate now just serves as a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To serve as' is a link phrase joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a specimen or instance that illustrates a point.

clue.text: Malay's pronounced ill feeling

indicators.note: said out loud, so the clue's Malay's gives a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a Malay is a person from Malaysia; with the possessive it sounds like the French-derived word for unease

explanation.surface: A man from Malaysia says he feels unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' signals the sound-alike: MALAY'S said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general sense of discomfort or unease, a vague ill feeling.

clue.text: Most are composed for him to conduct

definitions.text: Most are composed for him to conduct

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Most pieces of music are written for a conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' signals the anagram of MOSTARE, and the whole clue also defines a conductor, for whom most music is written.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished conductor of orchestras, the person who directs the performance.

clue.text: One sort of trust small investors may rely on?

definitions.meaning: a single item, one thing

definitions.text: sort of trust small investors may rely on?
definitions.meaning: a pooled investment fund sold in shares, popular with small savers in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: A unit trust is a British pooled investment fund, roughly a mutual fund.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a single whole, and also names a pooled investment fund sold in portions.

clue.text: Stories with stern endings they say

indicators.note: people saying it out loud, so the words that follow give a sound-alike

parts.note: tails are the rear ends, sterns, of animals

explanation.surface: Narratives with grim conclusions, so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern endings' looks like grim conclusions to stories, but means rear ends: TAILS, which 'they say' turns into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales are narratives or accounts, so they are stories.

clue.text: Knock out nuts after having turned them

indicators.note: turning the nuts round means the word nuts is read from its far end

explanation.surface: Someone is floored after tightening some bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having turned them' reverses NUTS; 'after' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to make them unconscious with a blow.

clue.text: Fellow so ill-bred as to hoot the queen

parts.note: to boo is to jeer, as a hoot is
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A man so badly brought up that he jeers at the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As to' joins the definition to the wordplay; R (Regina) is the usual crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A boor is a rude, uncouth man lacking manners.

clue.text: Common prison commotion

definitions.meaning: slang, or common, word for jail
a fuss or disturbance

explanation.definitionFit: The slang word for jail is also a noun for a fuss or a disturbance.

clue.text: Like rival businesses once entries have been accepted

definitions.meaning: firms that are rivals are vying with each other in the market
a contest is under way, and a submitted entry is part of the contest

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes firms vying for trade and also an entry taking part in a contest once accepted.

clue.text: What one can see of Hull is enjoyed by non-paying guests

definitions.text: What one can see of Hull
definitions.meaning: the part of a ship's side above the waterline, measured from deck to water
meals and lodging given without charge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' looks like the Yorkshire port city, but it is a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautical term is the height of a ship's side above the waterline, and also, split in two, food and lodging given at no cost.
